I've heard good things about Western Governors University. Their tuition is a flat fee that is very affordable if you're able to push through it as fast as possible, but isn't so great if you want to take your time. As with all online options, it's well suited for people who can't attend classes on campus for whatever reason.

Regardless of whether you decide to attend an online college/university or a traditional one, it's important to know the difference between regional and national accreditation. Credits from regionally accredited colleges and universities will generally transfer to other schools, whereas credits from nationally accredited colleges will pretty much never transfer. It's my personal opinion that nationally accredited colleges are a scam and are worthless. Their value technically isn't zero and there may be some uncommon unusual circumstances that may make them an appropriate choice, but as far as I'm concerned they should be avoided like the plague.
